generatedProse.concept-context: In practice, assessment turns up in more places than most students expect: not only exams and essays, but presentations, portfolios, reports, problem sets and seminar contributions. Some of it counts towards your final mark and some is there to help you practise. Working out which kind a task is, and what standard it is judged against, tells you how much weight to give it and what the marker will be looking for.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two students are given the same draft essay to hand in for comments. It is a formative task: the tutor will mark up the draft, but the grade will not count. The graded essay comes later.

Student A sees that the draft does not count and puts little into it, handing in a rough attempt and barely reading the comments that come back. When the graded essay is due, Student A makes the same mistakes the comments had already flagged.

Student B treats the draft as a chance to find out what is not working yet. The comments point out a weak line of argument, so Student B reworks it before the graded essay. The final piece is stronger, because the formative task did its job.

Both students did the same formative task. Only Student B used what it is for: formative assessment is there to help you improve before the summative assessment that sets your grade.
generatedProse.summary: Assessment at university is far wider than exams: essays, presentations, portfolios, reflective pieces, practice-based tasks and exams are all ways your work is judged against your subject’s standards. You can now tell formative assessment, which helps you improve and does not count, from summative assessment, which sets your grade. More than that, you can see how they work together: formative tasks are where you find out what is not yet working and put it right, so that by the time a summative task counts you are already performing at your best. This is what strategic learning means: recognising why each task has been set and what it is preparing you to do, because every formative and summative task is a step towards the same thing, being able to demonstrate your module’s learning outcomes. Once you can see that link, you can tell what any task is really asking of you and put your effort where it counts, in every module you take.

check.body: Sort each of these assessments by whether it is formative or summative.

items.text: A practice essay your tutor comments on but does not mark
A short quiz during term that does not count toward your grade
The final coursework essay that sets your module grade

feedback.correct: That's right. Formative assessment is there to help you improve and does not count toward your grade; summative assessment is the task that sets it.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. For each one, ask: does this count toward my final grade, or is it there to help me improve first?
feedback.incorrectFinal: The practice essay and the term quiz are formative: they help you improve and do not count. The examination and the final coursework essay are summative: they set your grade. The test is simple - does it count toward the mark, or help you reach it?
feedback.partlyCorrectNotFinal: Some of those are right, but not all. Check each one against the question: does it count, or help you improve first?
feedback.partlyCorrectFinal: Formative tasks (the practice essay, the term quiz) help you improve and do not count; summative tasks (the examination, the final coursework essay) set your grade.
